**Title**  
Remove the obsolete test “injection” command and its group registration  

**Problem**  
An example command was added solely for breaking‑test scenarios, exposing a set of deliberately unsafe completions. Its presence in the shipped CLI does not serve any functional purpose and may confuse users or be mistaken for a production feature.

- Eliminate the “injection” command from the command hierarchy.  
- Remove the registration of the command from the root configuration.  
- Delete the “Test Commands” group from the root command’s group list.  
- Ensure the CLI’s help output no longer lists the command or the test group.  
- Preserve the functionality of all remaining commands and groups.  

**Risk & Validation**  
- Verify that the removal does not break any existing documentation or integration tests that reference the command.  
- Run the full test suite and confirm all tests pass.  
- Manually inspect the `--help` output to ensure the command and test group are absent while other groups remain intact.

Please solve this issue in the repository scrapy/scrapy.

## Issue

**Title**  
Add Unicode email support, correct engine idle detection, improve Python 3 cookie handling, fix sitemap parsing, and deprecate bundled pydispatch  

**Problem**  
The email utility could not send non‑ASCII content, the execution engine could report idle incorrectly, the cookie wrapper lacked Python 3‑compatible attributes, sitemap parsing used raw bytes from *robots.txt*, and the internal copy of pydispatch is outdated.  

**Root Cause**  
Missing charset handling and overly compact idle logic, Python‑2‑centric cookie API, use of `response.body` instead of decoded text, and continued shipping of a deprecated bundled library.  

**Fix / Expected Behavior**  
- Email sender accepts an optional charset and encodes the message body and attachments accordingly.  
- Engine reports idle only when scraper, downloader, scheduler and start‑request processing are all exhausted.  
- Cookie wrapper provides properties (`host`, `type`, `origin_req_host`, etc.) matching the standard request interface on Python 3.  
- Sitemap spider parses *robots.txt* using decoded text, preventing Unicode handling errors.  
- Importing the old `scrapy.xlib.pydispatch` path now emits a deprecation warning and directs users to use the external `pydispatch` package.  

**Risk & Validation**  
- Run existing email tests to ensure default (ASCII) behavior remains unchanged.  
- Execute idle‑detection test suite to confirm spiders no longer shut down prematurely.  
- Add/verify tests for the new cookie properties on Python 3.  
- Validate that sitemap discovery still works with typical *robots.txt* files.  
- Check that the deprecation warning is raised without breaking imports in legacy code.

## Relevant Interface

Method: WrappedRequest.full_url(self)  
Location: scrapy/http/cookies.py → class WrappedRequest  
Inputs: None (uses the wrapped ``scrapy.Request`` instance)  
Outputs: ``str`` – the full URL of the wrapped request (identical to ``request.url``)  
Description: Read‑only property exposing ``request.url`` for Python‑3 compatibility; use when the URL of the original request is needed.

Method: WrappedRequest.host(self)  
Location: scrapy/http/cookies.py → class WrappedRequest  
Inputs: None (uses the wrapped ``scrapy.Request`` instance)  
Outputs: ``str`` – the network location part of the request URL (``urlparse(request).netloc``)  
Description: Property returning the host component of the request URL; replaces the old ``get_host()`` method.

Method: WrappedRequest.type(self)  
Location: scrapy/http/cookies.py → class WrappedRequest  
Inputs: None (uses the wrapped ``scrapy.Request`` instance)  
Outputs: ``str`` – the scheme (``http``, ``https``, etc.) of the request URL (``urlparse(request).scheme``)  
Description: Property returning the URL scheme; replaces the old ``get_type()`` method.

Method: WrappedRequest.origin_req_host(self)  
Location: scrapy/http/cookies.py → class WrappedRequest  
Inputs: None (uses the wrapped ``scrapy.Request`` instance)  
Outputs: ``str`` – the hostname part of the request URL (``urlparse_cached(request).hostname``)  
Description: Property exposing the origin request host; mirrors the old ``get_origin_req_host()`` method.

Function: MailSender.send(to, subject, body, cc=None, attachs=(), mimetype='text/plain', charset=None, _callback=None)  
Location: scrapy/mail.py → class MailSender  
Inputs:  
- ``to`` (list/iterable of email addresses) – recipients;  
- ``subject`` (str) – email subject;  
- ``body`` (str) – email body content;  
- ``cc`` (optional list) – carbon‑copy recipients;  
- ``attachs`` (optional iterable of ``(filename, mimetype, fileobj)``) – attachments;  
- ``mimetype`` (str, default ``'text/plain'``) – MIME type for the body;  
- ``charset`` (optional str) – character encoding for the message (e.g., ``'utf-8'``);  
- ``_callback`` (optional callable) – called after the message is prepared with keyword args containing ``msg`` and other details.  
Outputs: ``None`` (message is sent or, in debug mode, passed to ``_callback``).  
Description: Sends an e‑mail, now supporting a ``charset`` argument that sets the message charset (defaults to ``us-ascii`` when omitted) and adjusts the ``Content‑Type`` header accordingly; also propagates the charset to multipart messages when attachments are present.

Outputs: Import succeeds but immediately raises a ``ScrapyDeprecationWarning`` with the message “Importing from scrapy.xlib.pydispatch is deprecated …”.  
Description: Legacy compatibility layer that warns users that the bundled ``scrapy.xlib.pydispatch`` module is deprecated and they should import ``pydispatch`` directly; the warning is emitted on module import.

Outputs: Generator yielding ``scrapy.Request`` objects, each pointing to a discovered sitemap URL.  
Description: Internal helper used by ``SitemapSpider`` to parse ``robots.txt`` files for ``Sitemap:`` entries and to recursively parse discovered sitemap files; returns a sequence of requests for each extracted sitemap URL.

;; An example of some possible linters using Fennel's --plugin option.

;; The first two linters here can only function on static module
;; use. For instance, this code can be checked because they use static
;; field access on a local directly bound to a require call:

;; (local m (require :mymodule))
;; (print m.field) ; fails if mymodule lacks a :field field
;; (print (m.function 1 2 3)) ; fails unless mymodule.function takes 3 args

;; However, these cannot:

;; (local m (do (require :mymodule)) ; m is not directly bound
;; (print (. m field)) ; not a static field reference
;; (let [f m.function]
;;   (print (f 1 2 3)) ; intermediate local, not a static field call on m

;; Still, pretty neat, huh?

;; This file is provided as an example and is not part of Fennel's public API.

(fn save-require-meta [from to scope]
  "When destructuring, save module name if local is bound to a `require' call.
Doesn't do any linting on its own; just saves the data for other linters."
  (when (and (sym? to) (not (multi-sym? to)) (list? from)
             (sym? (. from 1)) (= :require (tostring (. from 1)))
             (= :string (type (. from 2))))
    (let [meta (. scope.symmeta (tostring to))]
      (set meta.required (tostring (. from 2))))))

(fn check-module-fields [symbol scope]
  "When referring to a field in a local that's a module, make sure it exists."
  (let [[module-local field] (or (multi-sym? symbol) [])
        module-name (-?> scope.symmeta (. (tostring module-local)) (. :required))
        module (and module-name (require module-name))]
    (assert-compile (or (= module nil) (not= (. module field) nil))
                    (string.format "Missing field %s in module %s"
                                   (or field :?) (or module-name :?)) symbol)))

(fn arity-check? [module] (-?> module getmetatable (. :arity-check?)))

(fn arity-check-call [[f & args] scope]
  "Perform static arity checks on static function calls in a module."
  (let [arity (# args)
        last-arg (. args arity)
        [f-local field] (or (multi-sym? f) [])
        module-name (-?> scope.symmeta (. (tostring f-local)) (. :required))
        module (and module-name (require module-name))]
    (when (and (arity-check? module) _G.debug _G.debug.getinfo
               (not (varg? last-arg)) (not (list? last-arg)))
      (assert-compile (= (type (. module field)) :function)
                      (string.format "Missing function %s in module %s"
                                     (or field :?) module-name) f)
      (match (_G.debug.getinfo (. module field))
        {: nparams :what "Lua" :isvararg true}
        (assert-compile (<= nparams (# args))
                        (: "Called %s.%s with %s arguments, expected %s+"
                           :format f-local field arity nparams) f)
        {: nparams :what "Lua" :isvararg false}
        (assert-compile (= nparams (# args))
                        (: "Called %s.%s with %s arguments, expected %s"
                           :format f-local field arity nparams) f)))))

(fn check-unused [ast scope]
  (each [symname (pairs scope.symmeta)]
    (assert-compile (or (. scope.symmeta symname :used) (symname:find "^_"))
                    (string.format "unused local %s" (or symname :?)) ast)))

{:destructure save-require-meta
 :symbol-to-expression check-module-fields
 :call arity-check-call
 ;; Note that this will only check unused args inside functions and let blocks,
 ;; not top-level locals of a chunk.
 :fn check-unused
 :do check-unused}
